items.topic: Data fetching route for agent-manager events
items.context: The swarm-manager UI needs to fetch run events from agent-manager. There are two approaches: proxy through swarm-manager's own API (which already has basic agent-manager integration via /agent-manager/runs/{id}), or call agent-manager directly. Per project feedback, client-side URL computation for cross-scenario routing is prohibited.

options.label: Proxy through swarm-manager API
options.rationale: Add a new endpoint like GET /api/v1/agent-manager/runs/{id}/events on swarm-manager API that proxies to agent-manager. Consistent with existing /agent-manager/runs/{id} pattern. UI only talks to its own backend. Recommended because it follows established patterns and avoids cross-origin issues.

options.label: Direct call to agent-manager with backend-provided URL
options.rationale: Have swarm-manager API return the agent-manager base URL in its status/config response, then the UI calls agent-manager directly. Reduces proxy overhead but adds cross-origin complexity and a second API dependency in the UI.

items.context: Agent-manager produces 8+ event types: message, tool_call, tool_result, log, status, metric, artifact, error, compaction. Showing everything could be noisy. The prompt-manager reference shows a curated events view.

options.label: Core conversation events only (message, tool_call, tool_result)
options.rationale: Cleanest UX — focuses on the actual agent conversation. Tool calls show what the agent did. Minimal noise.

options.label: Conversation + status + error events
options.rationale: Adds status transitions and errors for debugging context without the noise of metrics/logs. Recommended as a good balance of signal and completeness.

options.label: All event types with filtering controls
options.rationale: Show everything with toggle filters per event type. Most flexible but most complex to build and potentially overwhelming.

items.topic: Tab layout approach for execution details
items.context: The current ExecutionDetailsPage renders all sections in a single scrollable view (status card, post-run checks, prompt trace). Adding a Messages section requires restructuring to tabs or keeping the linear layout with a new section.

options.label: Radix Tabs with Overview + Messages
options.rationale: Clean separation. Overview tab contains current content. Messages tab is dedicated to conversation. Follows the prompt-manager RunEditorPanel pattern (Info/Events/Investigation tabs). Recommended because it matches existing UI patterns in the codebase.

options.label: Collapsible section at the bottom
options.rationale: Add an expandable 'Agent Messages' section below existing content. Simpler change, no layout restructuring, but could make the page very long.

items.topic: Pagination strategy for large event streams
items.context: Agent runs can produce hundreds or thousands of events. The agent-manager API supports sequence-based cursor pagination (after_sequence + limit). The UI needs a loading strategy.

options.label: Fetch all events on tab mount
options.rationale: Simplest implementation. Fine for small-medium runs (<200 events). Could be slow for large runs.

options.label: Paginated with 'Load more' button
options.rationale: Fetch initial page (e.g., 50 events), show 'Load more' at the bottom. User controls when to fetch more. Simple UX, predictable performance. Recommended for simplicity.

options.label: Infinite scroll with intersection observer
options.rationale: Automatically loads next page as user scrolls near the bottom. Smoother UX but more complex to implement correctly with event ordering.

items.text: The ExecutionRecord already has a `runId` field that links to the agent-manager run. The swarm-manager CLI also has basic agent-manager integration in `cmd_agent_manager.go` with types in `types.go`, though it currently only supports status, get-run, and stop-run — no event fetching. The proxy endpoint would need to be added to the swarm-manager API.
